description.p: Zeroize erases attached drives to a purge-grade standard and issues a PDF certificate recording what was destroyed, how, and on which machine.

It reads each drive's own capability registers and offers only the erase methods that drive will actually accept - NVMe Sanitize and Format NVM where the controller supports them, ATA Secure Erase for SATA drives that are not frozen, SCSI Sanitize for SAS, and multi-pass software overwrite as a universal fallback. Methods a drive cannot use are shown greyed out with the reason, rather than hidden.
The drive carrying the running system, and the live medium Zeroize itself booted from, are detected and can never be selected.

ul.li: NVMe Sanitize - crypto erase, block erase and overwrite
NVMe Format NVM - cryptographic erase (SES=2) and user data erase (SES=1)
ATA Secure Erase, standard and enhanced
SCSI Sanitize - crypto and block erase
Overwrite - single pass, DoD 5220.22-M (3 and 7 pass), HMG IS5, VSITR, Gutmann

description.p: The certificate now carries the project URL, so a reader who was not present at the erase can trace the document back to the build that produced it.
